valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 16 Nov 2026. (1) Business: two parts. Building materials (tiles, bathware, aluminium, packaging) and a 26.08% stake in LB Finance PLC, a finance company. Weighted by their share of 2025/26 owners' profit (Annual Report 2025/26, pp. 218, 255): LB Finance Rs 3.64bn of Rs 6.97bn = 52%; the operating businesses (after minorities, incl. Delmege) 48%. (2) Damodaran's emerging-markets dataset (betaEmerg) could NOT be opened: his site is blocked by this run's network settings. Stand-ins from web-search extracts: Building Materials global unlevered, cash-corrected 0.90 (date not shown in the extract); Financial Svcs. (Non-bank & Insurance) US levered 0.97 (176 firms, apparently January 2026). (3) Building materials relevered with net debt Rs 31.67bn (30 Sep 2026) ÷ market value Rs 53.29bn (Rs 48.10 × 1,107.9mn shares) = 0.59 and 29% tax: 0.90 × (1 + 0.71 × 0.59) = 1.28. The finance stake uses the sector's levered beta without relevering, as the brief says for finance companies. Weighted: 0.48 × 1.28 + 0.52 × 0.97 = 1.12. (4) Local 5-year betas: only one found, StockAnalysis 0.32 (5Y, about February 2026, web-search extract; the page couldn't be opened). Fewer than the 3 sources the rule asks for, so step 4 can't be completed. (5) Higher of 1.12 and 0.32 = 1.12. (6) Within 0.3–2. (7) Into the formula by scripts/reinvestment.py. Provisional: refresh in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets file and three verified local 5-year betas. The low local beta (0.32) suggests the market treats RCL as less risky than the sector figures imply; at a beta of 0.8 fair value would be roughly 30% higher on the book-based methods.

valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (16 Nov 2026): cost of debt 9.26% (interest paid 2.652 ÷ average borrowings and leases 28.63, FY 2026), tax 29%, debt weight 37.3% (net debt Rs 31.67bn at Sep 2026, market cap Rs 53.29bn at Rs 48.10).

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 2% / 4% / 6% (operating businesses); supported 0.7% (reinvestment rate 8.4% × return on capital 8.3%, FY 2026). Base 3.3 and bull 5.3 pts above: kept because FY 2026 reinvestment was unusually low after a heavy FY 2025 (capex 4.3bn vs depreciation 2.9bn, 5.2bn into working capital) and H1 FY2027 has already put about 5bn more into stock; revenue grew 14% in FY 2026 on existing capacity; and the DCF charges growth ÷ return on capital (8–11%) in reinvestment every year, so growth adds almost no value. Profit kept × ROE gives 9.1%, but that includes LB Finance's retained profit.
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py on the FY 2026 figures.

changeLog.basedOn: Annual Report 2025/26 and interims to 30 Jun and 30 Sep 2026 (CSE downloads)
changeLog.summary: Requested from Telegram (/add RCL.N0000). First analysis. Research record built from the three downloaded reports (FY 2025 and FY 2026 annual figures, reinvestment figures, Q1, Q2 and H1 FY2027). Beta 1.12 (provisional; Damodaran stand-ins from web search, one local 5-year beta of 0.32) gives cost of equity 19.8% and WACC 14.9%. Methods: sum of the parts (operating DCF at WACC less net debt, owners' 68%, plus associates at book) 22.1, P/E 30.8, justified P/B 29.7, residual income 26.4. Business tests 2 of 4 (fails returns and cash): category 3, avoid for now. Price Rs 48.10 is a web quote (Fiscal.ai, 12 Nov 2026), not the CSE close; LB Finance market value from early August 2026; 2024/25 capex booked and group figures before 2024/25 not available. Fair value Rs 27.20, buy Rs 23.10, strong buy Rs 20.40.
